questions: Tell me something about your secondary school.
Which subject did you find most difficult at school? [Why?]
Do you ever need that subject now? [Why? / Why not?]
What did you enjoy about being a school student?
Are there any famous buildings in your home town? [What are they?]
In what type of building do most people in your home town live?
Should buildings be attractive to look at? [Why? / Why not?]
What is the most unusual building you have ever seen? [Why?]

part2.title: Describe an interesting story that you heard or read about in the news.
points: when you heard or read about the story
what the story was about
why the story was in the news
part2.final: and explain why you thought the story was interesting.

questions: When do people like to read the newspaper?
How important is it for people to have a choice of newspaper?
What does a 'good' newspaper contain?
Why do some people choose to read the news on the Internet rather than in a newspaper?
How is Internet news different from the news you read in the newspaper?
Will Internet news ever replace newspapers? [Why? / Why not?]
Is your home town a good place to live? [Why? / Why not?]
What sort of jobs do people do in your home town?
In which part of your home town do most people live?
Where did you play in your home town when you were a child?
How often do you go to the cinema?
Do you prefer to watch a film at the cinema or at home? [Why?]
Which film from your childhood do you remember most? [Why?]
What's your favourite film now? [Why?]

part2.title: Describe an interesting place that you have visited as a tourist.
points: where this place is
why you went there
what you did there
part2.final: and explain why you thought this place was so interesting.

questions: What areas of a town or city do tourists often like to visit?
How important is it for local governments to look after popular tourist attractions?
Should people pay to visit attractions such as museums and galleries? [Why? / Why not?]
How should tourists behave when they are in a different country?
What can local people do to help tourists enjoy their visit?
What can tourists learn from visiting new places?

part1.intro: Let's talk about what you do. Do you work or are you a student?
questions: (Work) Why did you choose your job?
(Work) What are your working hours?
(Work) Tell me something about the people who work with you.
(Work) What don't you like about your job?
(Study) Why did you choose your subject(s)?
(Study) When do you prefer to study on your own? [Why?]
(Study) Tell me something about the other students on your course.
(Study) What don't you like about your studies?

part1.intro: Let's go on to talk about sport.
questions: What sports are popular in your country?
Did you learn any sports at school? [Why? / Why not?]
How often do you watch sport? [Why not?]
Do you participate in any sports at the moment? [Which ones?]

part2.title: Describe a special event (e.g. a festival, carnival or other celebration) that takes place in your country.
points: when the event takes place
why it takes place
what people do
part2.final: and explain why the event is special.

questions: What sort of occasions do families and friends like to celebrate?
How important are celebrations in people's lives? [Why? / Why not?]
Should people have time off work for important celebrations? [Why? / Why not?]
Why do many people enjoy participating in national celebrations?
Have national celebrations become more or less important over time? [Why?]
What sort of things do you think countries will celebrate in the future?
What kind of place is your town/city?
What's the most interesting part of your town/city?
Has your town/city changed in any way in your life time? [How?]
Would you say your town/city is a good place for young people to live? [Why? / Why not?]
What kind of things do you prefer shopping for?
In what kind of places do you like to go shopping? [Why?]
What effect has online shopping had in your country?
What would you recommend that tourists buy from your country? [Why?]

part2.title: Describe a popular teacher that you know.
points: what this teacher looks like
what sort of person this teacher is
what this teacher helped you to learn
part2.final: and explain why this teacher is popular.

questions: What can schools do to help students prepare for the next stage in their lives?
What advice would you give to someone who doesn't like school?
What can schools teach children that they can't learn from their parents?
In general, what opportunities are available to students after they leave school?
How do you think school life differs from university life?
How important do you think it is for individuals to carry on learning after they have finished school and university?

part1.intro: Let's talk about what you do. Do you work or are you a student? [Examiner chooses appropriate questions.]
questions: (Work) What job do you do?
(Work) What skills do you need for your job?
(Work) What do you particularly like about your job?
(Study) What subject are you studying?
(Study) Why did you want to study that subject?
(Study) How long have you been studying (English/nursing/accountancy, etc.)?
How often do you watch television?
What kinds of television programmes are most popular in your country?
Is there anything you would like to change about television in your country? [Why? / Why not?]

part2.title: Describe a restaurant you enjoyed going to.
points: where the restaurant was
who you went with
what type of food you ate in this restaurant
part2.final: and explain why you thought the restaurant was good.

questions: Do you think that people eat healthier food than they did in the past? [Why? / Why not?]
How important do you think it is for families to eat meals together?
What effects has modern technology had on the food we eat?
Why do people go to restaurants when they want to celebrate important occasions?
Do you think that food prepared at home is always better than in restaurants?
Which are more popular in your country: fast food restaurants or traditional restaurants? [Why?]
Do most people live in houses or apartments in your country?
What do people usually do in their free time in your country?
What do you enjoy most about living in your country?
Would you say that your country is a good place to visit? [Why?]
What is your favourite meal?
Do you prefer to eat out or eat at home? [Why?]
Are there any traditional meals that you would recommend? [Why?]
How have people's eating habits changed in your country?

part2.title: Describe a television programme that you watch.
points: which kind of television programme it is
what usually happens in the television programme
why you enjoy watching the television programme
part2.final: and explain why you would recommend the television programme to other people.

part3.topic: The role of advertising on television
questions: How do you feel about the amount of advertising on television?
In what ways has television advertising changed in the last ten years?
To what extent are people influenced by the advertising they see on television?

part3.topic: The effect of films on society
questions: Why do people still enjoy going to the cinema to watch a film?
What sort of influence can films have on people?
Should film-makers be responsible for the impact their films can have on people?
Can you find food from many different countries where you live? [Why/Why not?]
How often do you eat typical food from other countries? [Why/Why not?]
Have you ever tried making food from another country? [Why/Why not?]
What food from your country would you recommend to people from other countries? [Why?]

part2.title: Describe a law that was introduced in your country and that you thought was a very good idea.
points: what the law was
who introduced it
when and why it was introduced
part2.final: and explain why you thought this law was such a good idea.

questions: What kinds of rules are common in a school?
How important is it to have rules in a school?
What do you recommend should happen if children break school rules?
Can you suggest why many students decide to study law at university?
What are the key personal qualities needed to be a successful lawyer?
Do you agree that working in the legal profession is very stressful?
Have you travelled a lot by plane? [To where?/Why not?]
Why do you think some people enjoy travelling by plane?
Would you like to live near an airport? [Why/Why not?]
In the future, do you think that you will travel by plane more often? [Why/Why not?]

part2.title: Describe a person from your country who has won a prize, award or medal.
points: who this person is
which prize, award or medal they received
what they did to win this
part2.final: and explain whether you think it was right that this person received this prize, award or medal.

questions: What types of school prizes do children in your country receive?
What do you think are the advantages of rewarding schoolchildren for good work?
Do you agree that it's more important for children to receive rewards from their parents than from teachers?
Do you think that some sportspeople (e.g., top footballers) are paid too much money?
Should everyone on a team get the same prize money when they win?
Do you agree with the view that, in sport, taking part is more important than winning?
Do you prefer spending holidays with friends or with family? [Why?]
What kind of holiday accommodation do you like to stay in? [Why?]
What plans do you have for your next holiday?
Is your city or region a good place for other people to visit on holiday? [Why/Why not?]

part2.title: Describe a car journey you made that took longer than expected.
points: where you were going
who you were with
how you felt during the journey
part2.final: and explain why this car journey took longer than expected.

questions: How interested are young people in your country in learning to drive?
What are the differences between driving in the countryside and driving in the city?
Do you consider most drivers where you live to be good drivers?
How popular are electric cars in your country?
In what ways could more people be persuaded to buy electric cars?
Do you think all cars will be electric one day?
Do you have a favourite café? [Why/Why not?]
Do you often go to cafés by yourself? [Why/Why not?]
What do you think helps to make a café very popular? [Why?]
Why do some people prefer cafés that are part of large chains, rather than small, local cafés?

part2.title: Describe a place you visited that has beautiful views.
points: where this place is
when and why you visited it
what views you can see from this place
part2.final: and explain why you think these views are so beautiful.

questions: Do you agree that most beauty products are a waste of money?
How does the beauty industry advertise its products so successfully?
What do you think of the view that beauty products should not be advertised to children?
Why do many people equate youth with beauty?
Do you think that being beautiful could affect a person's success in life?
Why might society's ideas about beauty change over time?
What kinds of bills do you have to pay?
How do you usually pay your bills – in cash or by another method? [Why?]
Have you ever forgotten to pay a bill? [Why/Why not?]
Is there anything you could do to make your bills cheaper? [Why/Why not?]

part2.title: Describe some food or drink that you learned to prepare.
points: what food or drink you learned to prepare
when and where you learned to prepare this
how you learned to prepare this
part2.final: and explain how you felt about learning to prepare this food or drink.

questions: What kinds of things can children learn to cook?
Do you think it is important for children to learn to cook?
Do you think young people should learn to cook at home or at school?
How enjoyable do you think it would be to work as a professional chef?
What skills does a person need to be a great chef?
How much influence do celebrity/TV chefs have on what ordinary people cook?

What do you remember about your science teachers at school?
How interested are you in science now? [Why/Why not?]
What do you think has been an important recent scientific development? [Why?]

part2.title: Describe a tourist attraction in your country that you would recommend.
points: what the tourist attraction is
where in your country this tourist attraction is
what visitors can see and do at this tourist attraction
part2.final: and explain why you would recommend this tourist attraction.

questions: What are the most popular museums and art galleries in … / where you live?

part2.title: Describe a time when you enjoyed visiting a member of your family in their home.

why you made this visit
what happened during this visit

questions: When do families celebrate together in your country?

How many hours do you usually sleep at night?
Do you sometimes sleep during the day? [Why/Why not?]

part2.title: Describe a time when you met someone who you became good friends with.
points: who you met
when and where you met this person
what you thought about this person when you first met

when and why you visited it

what you bought from this website
how satisfied you were with what you bought
